report_name: Pentagon Reveals Breach; Kiteworks Halts Systems on Threat Intel

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: Attackers compromised the Defense Manpower Data Center by exploiting a trusted relationship with a third-party data service provider.

attack_patterns.name: Supply Chain Compromise
attack_patterns.description: The breach of the Pentagon's DMDC was a classic supply chain attack, where a less secure third-party vendor was compromised to access the primary target's data.

attack_patterns.name: Automated Exfiltration
attack_patterns.description: Attackers had a long dwell time of several months, providing ample opportunity to exfiltrate sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of U.S. military and federal personnel.

tools.name: Kiteworks Platform
tools.description: A secure file transfer appliance which had a previously unknown critical vulnerability discovered and patched in September 2026 following a proactive, customer-wide shutdown.

vulnerabilities.name: Kiteworks Critical Vulnerability September 2026
vulnerabilities.description: A previously unknown critical vulnerability discovered and patched by Kiteworks during a proactive shutdown in September 2026. The flaw affected a feature used by less than 1% of customers and was patched before any evidence of exploitation.

campaigns.name: Pentagon DMDC Breach October 2025
campaigns.description: A data breach campaign targeting the U.S. Department of Defense's Defense Manpower Data Center via a third-party contractor in October 2025, resulting in the compromise of personnel PII.
campaigns.objective: Steal sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of U.S. military and federal personnel.

identities.name: U.S. Department of Defense
identities.description: Victim of a major data breach discovered months after it occurred in October 2025. The breach occurred via a third-party contractor connected to the Defense Manpower Data Center.

identities.name: Defense Manpower Data Center
identities.description: A data center within the U.S. Department of Defense whose data, including sensitive personnel information, was compromised in a supply chain attack.

identities.name: Kiteworks
identities.description: A secure file transfer company (formerly Accellion) that proactively advised customers to shut down systems based on federal threat intelligence, allowing it to discover and patch a critical zero-day vulnerability before exploitation.

identities.name: U.S. military and federal personnel
identities.description: Class of individuals whose Personally Identifiable Information (PII), including Social Security numbers and employment details, was potentially exposed in the Defense Manpower Data Center breach.

indicators.name: Anomalous Data Transfer Volume to Third-Party Vendor
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Data Transfer Volume to Third-Party Vendor
id: 7e8b1c2d-3a4f-4b5c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: Detects anomalous volumes or patterns of data transfer between an internal network and known third-party vendors, which could indicate a supply chain compromise or data exfiltration.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-28
references:
  - https://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/pentagon-data-breach-and-kiteworks-targeted-in-cyberattacks/
level: medium
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate large data transfers, backups, or initial data synchronization.
tags:
  - attack.t1195
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    action: 'allow'
    # Placeholder for known third-party vendor IP ranges
    dst_ip|cidr:
      - 1.2.3.0/24
  # This rule requires a baseline of normal traffic volume to be effective.
  # The condition would be implemented in the SIEM logic (e.g., 'count > threshold over time').
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Monitors and baselines all connections between the internal network and third-party vendors, alerting on anomalous volumes or patterns of data transfer that could indicate exfiltration.

indicators.name: Suspicious Egress from Secure File Transfer Appliance
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Egress from Secure File Transfer Appliance
id: 8f9a0b1c-2d3e-4f5a-6b7c-8d9e0f1a2b3c
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound traffic from a secure file transfer appliance to an unknown or suspicious destination, which could indicate data exfiltration or C2 communication.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-28
references:
  - https://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/pentagon-data-breach-and-kiteworks-targeted-in-cyberattacks/
level: high
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate, newly configured external destinations.
tags:
  - attack.t1020
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    # Placeholder for the source IP of the secure file transfer appliance
    c-ip: '192.168.1.100'
  filter_known_dest:
    # Placeholder for known legitimate destinations
    cs-host|endswith:
      - '.trustedpartner.com'
      - '.anotherpartner.net'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_dest
indicators.description: Identifies any outbound traffic from a secure file transfer appliance to an unknown or suspicious destination, which should be treated as a high-priority alert.
